subproblem.title: Gram determinant on a subspace equals the determinant of the compressed operator p A* A p + (I − p)
subproblem.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ and E := ℝ^P (Euclid P) with its standard inner product ⟨·,·⟩. Let V be a linear subspace of E, p := V.starProjection the orthogonal projection of E onto V, I the identity of E, ι a finite type with decidable equality, e = (e_i)_{i∈ι} an orthonormal basis of V, and A : E → E a continuous linear map with adjoint A*. Then det(⟨A e_i, A e_j⟩)_{i,j∈ι} = det(p ∘ (A* ∘ A) ∘ p + (I − p)), where the right-hand side is the determinant of this endomorphism of E.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (V : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)) {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (e : OrthonormalBasis ι ℝ V) (A : Euclid P →L[ℝ] Euclid P), Matrix.det (Matrix.of fun i j : ι => inner ℝ (A (e i)) (A (e j))) = (V.starProjection ∘L (A.adjoint ∘L A) ∘L V.starProjection + (ContinuousLinearMap.id ℝ (Euclid P) - V.starProjection)).det
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 1 of the parent proof (the block-determinant identity behind J(x)² = det(p(x)Dφ(x)*Dφ(x)p(x) + I − p(x))), which is the fixed-dimension form of Simon's Ch. 3 formula 2.3, J^M_f(x) = sqrt(det J(x)) = sqrt(det(d^M f_x* ∘ d^M f_x)) with J(x) the Gram matrix of D_{τ_p} f · D_{τ_q} f in any orthonormal basis τ of T_x M (book/chapter-03.txt lines 362–369; formula 2.3 at line 365). Details are filled in below; the argument is the parent's ("T maps V into V and is the identity on V^⊥, so det T is the determinant of T|_V, whose matrix in e is G").

Notation. E := Euclid P = ℝ^P with its standard inner product ⟨·,·⟩. V ≤ E is a subspace; it is finite-dimensional, so V.HasOrthogonalProjection holds and p := V.starProjection : E →L[ℝ] E (the orthogonal projection onto V) is defined. I := ContinuousLinearMap.id ℝ E, A* := A.adjoint, T := p ∘ (A* ∘ A) ∘ p + (I − p) : E →L[ℝ] E, and G := (⟨A e_i, A e_j⟩)_{i,j∈ι} = Matrix.of fun i j => ⟨A e_i, A e_j⟩. The right-hand side T.det is ContinuousLinearMap.det T, which is by definition LinearMap.det of the underlying linear map. The inner product of V is the restriction of that of E: ⟨(u : E), (w : E)⟩ = ⟨u, w⟩_V (Submodule.coe_inner).
Facts used. (P1) p x ∈ V for every x ∈ E (Submodule.starProjection_apply_mem). (P2) p v = v ⟺ v ∈ V (Submodule.starProjection_eq_self_iff). (P3) p w = 0 ⟺ w ∈ V^⊥ (Submodule.starProjection_apply_eq_zero_iff). (P4) ⟨p x, y⟩ = ⟨x, p y⟩ (Submodule.inner_starProjection_left_eq_right). (P5) ⟨x, A* y⟩ = ⟨A x, y⟩ (ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint_inner_right).

1. V is T-invariant. Let v ∈ V. By (P2), p v = v, so T v = p(A*(A(p v))) + (v − p v) = p(A*(A v)) + 0, which lies in V by (P1). Hence V ≤ V.comap T; call this hT and write T_V := T.restrict hT : V →ₗ[ℝ] V for the restriction of T to V (T_V u = T u as elements of E).

2. T is the identity modulo V, and on V^⊥. For every x ∈ E, T x − x = p(A*(A(p x))) − p x, a difference of two elements of V by (P1), hence an element of V. Therefore the map T̄ := V.mapQ V T hT induced by T on the quotient E/V sends the class [x] to [T x] = [x] (Submodule.Quotient.eq), i.e. T̄ = id_{E/V} (it suffices to check this on representatives, Submodule.linearMap_qext). Moreover, if w ∈ V^⊥ then p w = 0 by (P3), so T w = p(A*(A 0)) + (w − 0) = w.

3. det T = det T_V. Let f = (f_c)_{c∈κ} be an orthonormal basis of V^⊥ (for instance stdOrthonormalBasis ℝ V^⊥). Since E is finite-dimensional, V and V^⊥ are complementary subspaces (V ⊓ V^⊥ = ⊥ and V ⊔ V^⊥ = ⊤; Submodule.isCompl_orthogonal), so the concatenated family b := (e, f), indexed by ι ⊕ κ, is a basis of E (indeed an orthonormal one). Compute the matrix of T in b column by column: the column at e_j consists of the coordinates of T e_j = T_V e_j, which lies in V by step 1, so its e-part is the j-th column of M := LinearMap.toMatrix e e T_V (the matrix of T_V in e) and its f-part is 0; the column at f_c is the coordinate vector of T f_c = f_c (step 2), i.e. 0 in the e-part and the c-th unit vector in the f-part. Hence the matrix of T in b is the block matrix fromBlocks M 0 0 1, and det T = det(LinearMap.toMatrix b b T) = det M · det 1 = det M = det T_V (LinearMap.det_toMatrix, Matrix.det_fromBlocks_zero₂₁, Matrix.det_one).
 Equivalent packaged form (this is how the verified formalization below proceeds, avoiding the construction of b): Mathlib's LinearMap.det_eq_det_mul_det, applied to the linear map T with W := V and the invariance hT, gives det T = det(T.restrict hT) · det(V.mapQ V T hT) (its instance side conditions Module.Finite ℝ E, Module.Free ℝ V, Module.Finite ℝ V and Module.Free ℝ (E ⧸ V) hold automatically over the field ℝ in finite dimension); by step 2, V.mapQ V T hT = id, whose determinant is 1 (LinearMap.det_id), so det T = det T_V.

4. The matrix of T_V in e is G. By LinearMap.det_toMatrix, det T_V = det(LinearMap.toMatrix e.toBasis e.toBasis T_V). Its (i, j) entry is the i-th coordinate of T_V e_j in the orthonormal basis e, namely ⟨e_i, T_V e_j⟩_V = ⟨(e_i : E), T (e_j : E)⟩ (LinearMap.toMatrix_apply, OrthonormalBasis.coe_toBasis, OrthonormalBasis.coe_toBasis_repr_apply, OrthonormalBasis.repr_apply_apply, Submodule.coe_inner, LinearMap.coe_restrict_apply). Since e_j ∈ V, p e_j = e_j by (P2), so T e_j = p(A*(A e_j)) + (e_j − e_j) = p(A*(A e_j)). Hence
 ⟨e_i, T e_j⟩ = ⟨e_i, p(A*(A e_j))⟩ = ⟨p e_i, A*(A e_j)⟩ (P4) = ⟨e_i, A*(A e_j)⟩ (P2, as e_i ∈ V) = ⟨A e_i, A e_j⟩ (P5) = G_{ij}.

5. Conclusion. By step 4, LinearMap.toMatrix e.toBasis e.toBasis T_V = G entrywise, so det G = det T_V, and by step 3 det T_V = det T = T.det. This is the asserted identity det(⟨A e_i, A e_j⟩)_{i,j} = (p ∘L (A* ∘L A) ∘L p + (I − p)).det. No case distinction is needed: if V = ⊥ then ι is empty, G is the empty matrix with determinant 1, and T = I has determinant 1, consistently with the argument.

Formalization note (complete script checked with `lake env lean` in this repository's pinned environment, Lean v4.35.0-rc3, Mathlib 25730c7c, inside `namespace GMT.Ch07` / `namespace Submission` with the frozen contract's `open`s; no errors, no warnings, axioms propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound):
  intro P V ι _ _ e A
  set p := V.starProjection with hp_def
  set T : Euclid P →L[ℝ] Euclid P := p ∘L (A.adjoint ∘L A) ∘L p + (ContinuousLinearMap.id ℝ (Euclid P) - p) with hT_def
  have hT : V ≤ V.comap (T : Euclid P →ₗ[ℝ] Euclid P) := by
    intro v hv
    have hpv : p v = v := Submodule.starProjection_eq_self_iff.mpr hv
    simp only [Submodule.mem_comap, ContinuousLinearMap.coe_coe, hT_def,
      add_apply, ContinuousLinearMap.comp_apply,
      sub_apply, ContinuousLinearMap.id_apply, hpv, sub_self, add_zero]
    exact V.starProjection_apply_mem _
  have hQ : V.mapQ V (T : Euclid P →ₗ[ℝ] Euclid P) hT = LinearMap.id := by
    apply Submodule.linearMap_qext
    ext x
    simp only [LinearMap.coe_comp, Function.comp_apply, Submodule.mkQ_apply,
      Submodule.mapQ_apply, LinearMap.id_comp]
    rw [Submodule.Quotient.eq]
    have : (T : Euclid P →ₗ[ℝ] Euclid P) x - x = p ((A.adjoint ∘L A) (p x)) - p x := by
      simp only [ContinuousLinearMap.coe_coe, hT_def, add_apply,
        ContinuousLinearMap.comp_apply, sub_apply,
        ContinuousLinearMap.id_apply]
      abel
    rw [this]
    exact V.sub_mem (V.starProjection_apply_mem _) (V.starProjection_apply_mem _)
  have hsplit := LinearMap.det_eq_det_mul_det V (T : Euclid P →ₗ[ℝ] Euclid P) hT
  rw [hQ, LinearMap.det_id, mul_one] at hsplit
  rw [ContinuousLinearMap.det, hsplit, ← LinearMap.det_toMatrix e.toBasis]
  congr 1
  ext i j
  rw [LinearMap.toMatrix_apply, OrthonormalBasis.coe_toBasis, OrthonormalBasis.coe_toBasis_repr_apply,
    OrthonormalBasis.repr_apply_apply, Matrix.of_apply]
  have hpj : p (e j) = e j := Submodule.starProjection_eq_self_iff.mpr (e j).2
  have hpi : p (e i) = e i := Submodule.starProjection_eq_self_iff.mpr (e i).2
  rw [Submodule.coe_inner, LinearMap.coe_restrict_apply]
  simp only [ContinuousLinearMap.coe_coe, hT_def, add_apply,
    ContinuousLinearMap.comp_apply, sub_apply,
    ContinuousLinearMap.id_apply, hpj, sub_self, add_zero]
  rw [← Submodule.inner_starProjection_left_eq_right, hpi, ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint_inner_right]
proof_key_steps: V is invariant under T := p∘(A*∘A)∘p + (I − p): for v ∈ V, p v = v so T v = p(A*A v) ∈ V.
T is the identity modulo V (T x − x = p(A*A p x) − p x ∈ V), hence induces id on E/V; and T w = w for w ∈ V^⊥ since p w = 0.

Block-triangular determinant over the invariant subspace V (matrix fromBlocks M 0 0 1 in the basis (e, f), f an orthonormal basis of V^⊥; packaged as LinearMap.det_eq_det_mul_det): det T = det(T|_V)·det(id) = det(T|_V).
The matrix of T|_V in e has entries ⟨e_i, T e_j⟩ = ⟨e_i, p A*A e_j⟩ = ⟨p e_i, A*A e_j⟩ = ⟨e_i, A*A e_j⟩ = ⟨A e_i, A e_j⟩, i.e. it is the Gram matrix G.
Hence det G = det(T|_V) = det T.
